title: Simulacrum: Splinters, the Item, and the 7-Wave Delirium Encounter in 0.5
summary: In Path of Exile 2 0.5, 300 Simulacrum Splinters auto-combine into an itemised Simulacrum (a currency item, not a Waystone). You then apply it to an Atlas map node at 100% or higher Deliriousness, inside your Delirium fog, turning that node into a Simulacrum of Delusion - a 7-wave encounter. This guide covers the current 0.5 flow, eligibility, between-wave shards, rewards, and the retired 15-wave / Realmgate version.
description: How the Simulacrum works in Path of Exile 2 0.5: 300 splinters into a Simulacrum item, applying it to a 100%+ Delirious Atlas map, the 7-wave Simulacrum of Delusion, Liquid Emotion rewards, and the historical 15-wave flow.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Path of Exile 2 Simulacrum item and the 0.5 flow: 300 Simulacrum Splinters, applying it to a 100% Delirious Atlas map, and the 7-wave Simulacrum of Delusion

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: In 0.5, a full stack of 300 Simulacrum Splinters auto-combines into an itemised Simulacrum - a currency item, not a Waystone. To run it, right-click the Simulacrum and left-click an Atlas map node that is at 100% or higher Deliriousness and inside your Delirium fog. That node becomes a Simulacrum of Delusion, a 7-wave encounter. Do NOT put it in the Map Device.
calloutDetail: The old 15-wave Simulacrum and the Realmgate flow are historical (pre-0.5) and no longer apply.
Reaching 100% Deliriousness is done by spreading Delirium fog (e.g. via a Grand Mirror) and clearing those foggy maps; the node then becomes a legal Simulacrum target.

answers.label: Use for
text: Running the 7-wave Simulacrum of Delusion for Liquid Emotions, Simulacrum-exclusive uniques, and a key toward the Delirium pinnacle.

answers.label: Check first
text: Confirm the target Atlas node is inside your fog and shows 100%+ Deliriousness before applying.

answers.label: Avoid
text: Trying to socket the Simulacrum into the Map Device like a Waystone, or applying it below 100% Deliriousness.

facts.label: Made from
note: Auto-combine in your inventory into a single itemised Simulacrum.

facts.label: Applied to
note: Must be inside your Delirium fog; right-click the item then left-click the node.

facts.label: Encounter
note: Deliriousness scales 100% at wave 1 up to 200% at wave 7. Old guides quoting 15 waves are pre-0.5.

facts.label: Item type
note: Not a Waystone; it cannot be placed in the Map Device.

facts.label: Consumed
note: The Simulacrum is spent when it transforms the node. Whether death refunds it is pending in-game verification.

facts.label: Tradeable
note: The itemised Simulacrum is account-bound; only the splinter stacks are commonly traded on the Currency Exchange.

sections.title: The 0.5 Simulacrum chain
intro: The current Simulacrum is a small chain of splinters, an item, and an encounter. The members below are what you handle; Delirium fog and the Grand Mirror are the ramp that gets a node to 100% Deliriousness.

members.title: Simulacrum Splinter
body: Drops from Delirium encounters on your maps. A full stack of 300 in your inventory auto-combines into an itemised Simulacrum.

members.title: Simulacrum (item)
body: The currency item formed from 300 splinters. Applied directly to a 100%+ Delirious Atlas node to open the encounter; not used in the Map Device.

members.title: Simulacrum of Delusion
body: The map that opens when you apply the item: 7 escalating waves of Delirium monsters, Deliriousness 100% to 200%.

members.title: Liquid Emotion
body: Each wave drops at least one Liquid Emotion; boss waves can drop higher-tier ones. Used to anoint amulets.

sections.title: How to get Simulacrum Splinters and the item
intro: Simulacrum Splinters come from Delirium content, and the itemised Simulacrum is what 300 of them become. You do not buy the item directly.

routes.label: Delirium encounters on maps
body: Run maps with a Delirium Mirror or instilled Delirium. Many current guides note splinters only drop once you have allocated the Delirium Atlas passive 'Is This About Me or You?'; confirm against your in-game Atlas tree.

routes.label: Ramp fog to 100% Deliriousness
body: Clearing foggy maps (spread via a Grand Mirror) raises each node Deliriousness %. At 100%, a fog node becomes a legal Simulacrum target, and 300 splinters auto-combine into the item.

routes.label: Combine 300 splinters
body: A full 300-splinter stack in your inventory auto-combines into one itemised Simulacrum. Splinters also trade on the Currency Exchange if your build cannot clear the waves.

routes.label: Quest version
body: The Delirium questline first grants access through Elder Madox and a quest Simulacrum of Delusion; the repeatable itemised Simulacrum is the farmable version.

sections.title: How to apply and run a Simulacrum

steps.label: Bank 300 Simulacrum Splinters
body: Farm Delirium until a full stack auto-combines into an itemised Simulacrum in your inventory.

steps.label: Reach 100%+ Deliriousness on a node
body: Spread Delirium fog across the Atlas (e.g. via a Grand Mirror) and clear those maps. Hover a fog node to confirm its Deliriousness % - it must read 100% or higher.

steps.label: Apply the Simulacrum to the node
body: Right-click the Simulacrum item, then left-click the 100%+ Delirious node inside your fog (on controller, open inventory over the node and apply it). It transforms into a Simulacrum of Delusion.

steps.label: Clear 7 waves
body: Enter the arena and survive 7 waves. Between waves you pick one Fracturing Shard effect (Escalating Threats, Apex Predators, or Pure Emotions) that applies to all remaining waves.

steps.label: Collect rewards
body: Each wave drops at least one Liquid Emotion; the final wave drops a Simulacrum-exclusive unique and 1-2 Raven's Reflection. Clearing wave 7 also grants Delirium Atlas points and a key toward the Delirium pinnacle.

before: Old flow (pre-0.5): a 15-wave Simulacrum opened via the Realmgate; the itemised Simulacrum was effectively removed.
after: Current flow (0.5): 300 splinters -> itemised Simulacrum -> applied to a 100%+ Delirious Atlas node -> 7-wave Simulacrum of Delusion.
compare.note: The Realmgate path is historical; current Simulacrums are applied directly to a Delirious Atlas node.

sections.title: Where a Simulacrum applies
note: A Simulacrum only applies to an Atlas map node that is inside your Delirium fog and at 100% or higher Deliriousness. It is never placed in the Map Device.

items.label: Full 300 splinters combined
checks: Confirm the itemised Simulacrum exists in your inventory, not loose splinter stacks.
items.why: Loose splinters below 300 will not open the encounter.
items.fix: Farm or buy splinters up to a full stack.

items.label: Node at 100%+ Deliriousness
checks: Hover the target node and read its Deliriousness %; it must be 100 or higher.
items.why: Below 100% the Simulacrum will not apply.
items.fix: Clear more foggy maps on that node to push it to 100%+.

items.label: Node inside your fog
checks: Confirm the node is covered by your Delirium fog bank.
items.why: A 100% node outside the fog is not a valid target.
items.fix: Spread fog onto the node with a Grand Mirror first.

items.label: Build can clear wave 7
checks: Verify your character survives 200% Deliriousness content before committing the item.
items.why: The Simulacrum is consumed on apply; a failed run wastes it.
items.fix: Sell the splinter stack instead if your build is not ready.

rows.benefit: Liquid Emotions, Simulacrum uniques, Raven's Reflection, pinnacle key
rows.recommendation: Run the 7-wave Simulacrum; highest currency ceiling in 0.5.
Clear wave 7 to obtain the key; pair with Kosis / Omniphobia drops for reliquary keys.
Sell the 300-splinter stack on the Currency Exchange instead.

rows.gain: Some Liquid Emotions from cleared waves
rows.loss: The Simulacrum is consumed; no pinnacle key
rows.recommendation: Only commit when your build can reach wave 7; otherwise sell the splinters.

sections.title: Current 0.5 flow vs the historical 15-wave Simulacrum
paragraphs: Current 0.5 flow: 300 Simulacrum Splinters (auto-combine in inventory) -> itemised Simulacrum -> applied to an Atlas map node at 100%+ Deliriousness inside your fog -> Simulacrum of Delusion, a 7-wave encounter (Deliriousness 100% at wave 1 rising to 200% at wave 7).

HISTORICAL (pre-0.5 - do not follow): the Simulacrum was a 15-wave encounter opened through the Realmgate, and the itemised Simulacrum was removed. Any guide quoting 15 waves or a Realmgate slot is using old Path of Exile 1 / pre-0.5 numbers.

Between waves in the current version you pick one Fracturing Shard effect (Escalating Threats adds a modifier, Apex Predators adds a boss, Pure Emotions adds monster packs) that applies to all remaining waves.
bullets: Current: item applied to a 100%+ Delirious Atlas node, 7 waves.
Historical: Realmgate, 15 waves, no itemised Simulacrum.
Any '15 waves / Realmgate' instruction is out of date for 0.5.

entries.question: Where do I open the Simulacrum in 0.5 - the Map Device does nothing?
summary: A player tried to socket the Simulacrum into the Map Device and it did not work.
editorialAnalysis: In 0.5 the Simulacrum is a currency item applied directly to a 100%+ Delirious Atlas node, not placed in the Map Device like a Waystone.
officialAnswer: Right-click the Simulacrum, then left-click a fog node at 100% or higher Deliriousness to transform it.

entries.question: I applied the Simulacrum on a 200% map and it turned into a Grand Mirror instead - why?
summary: A player was confused when a high-Deliriousness node behaved like a Grand Mirror interaction.
editorialAnalysis: A node at 100%+ Deliriousness is exactly the Simulacrum target, but the same fog bank is also what the Grand Mirror uses to spread fog. The transform happens when you apply the Simulacrum item specifically to that node; simply having 200% fog does not auto-open the encounter.
officialAnswer: Apply the itemised Simulacrum to the 100%+ node to open the encounter; the Grand Mirror is a separate fog-spreading interaction.

entries.question: My video shows 15 waves but the game only has 7 - which is right?
summary: A player saw conflicting wave counts between old videos and the current client.
editorialAnalysis: Patch 0.5 cut the Simulacrum from 15 waves to 7. Old videos quoting 15 waves are pre-0.5 and should be ignored for current mechanics.
officialAnswer: The current Simulacrum of Delusion is a 7-wave encounter.
